title: TransferRecord
description: A typed source object and its proposed target binding in one immutable staging revision.

id.description: Immutable identity allocated once by the interoperability owner.

job_id.x-reference-scope: Reference must resolve inside the owning Institution or the directly owned aggregate.

plan_revision.description: Immutable transfer plan revision that owns this candidate record. Never resolves against a newer plan implicitly.

source_layer.description: Independent source publication layer. Shared definitions have no draft or published-only selector.

record_role.description: Semantic source occurrence role. Reusable definitions and placements always have separate records.

occurrence_key.description: Stable source-scoped occurrence disambiguator. Use defined sentinel definition for a single non-occurrence record. An ambiguous move or reorder requires review.

reachability.description: Classification in the frozen selected root dependency closure. Detached and outside-selection rows do not certify publishability.

source_revision.description: Source snapshot key or content-derived revision.

source_locator.description: Archive relative path and node selector, not an arbitrary URL.

source_fingerprint.description: Digest of preserved source record identity, bytes and projection-relevant metadata.

target_id.description: Canonical target identity in the registered owner domain.

target_revision_id.description: Target immutable version or staged pointer.

baseline_target_digest.description: Target fingerprint used in three-way comparison.

disposition.description: Machine-produced coverage classification, review decision stored independently.

x-invariants: References stay within the job graph or an explicit authorized external map.
Protected drafts are not visible to learners.
Every processed or blocked source object contributes to the reconciliation totals.
A record and its typed TransferEdge relationships are immutable within a plan revision. Plan correction appends another revision.
An opaque source key is not a native UUID. Allocation uses approved scoped identity and occurrence, never a raw hexadecimal token or archive path.
Required selected reachability with an unresolved blocking issue prohibits promotion of the dependent root. Detached and outside-selection records remain in restricted inventory.
